name: Centerville
moldStory: Centerville mixes historic stone homes in Uptown (some on the National Register) with 1970s–90s subdivisions; older stone foundations wick moisture, while mature trees and shaded lots keep humidity high around foundations.
intro: Centerville is two towns in one: historic stone homes in Uptown — some on the National Register — alongside 1970s–90s subdivisions like Yankee Trace. The older stone foundations wick moisture upward through basement walls, while mature trees and shaded lots keep humidity high around foundations. In the newer subdivisions, the risk shifts to fast-built drainage and humid crawl spaces. Either way, moisture finds the weak point first.
moldNote: Centerville's dual housing stock splits the risk: wicking stone foundations in historic Uptown homes, and humid crawl spaces plus drainage quirks in the 1970s–90s subdivisions.

problemCards.title: Wicking stone foundations
problemCards.body: Historic stone foundations in Uptown draw moisture upward — basement walls stay damp for weeks after rain.

problemCards.title: Shaded-lot humidity
problemCards.body: Mature trees and shaded lots trap humidity around foundations, feeding crawl-space growth.

problemCards.title: Attic ventilation gaps
problemCards.body: Older rooflines with unbalanced ventilation trap winter moisture against sheathing.
